DEFECT (found on a real run). The narration hedge you added is INERT in the real game. `CloudflareTurnProvider._request_allowing_one_transient_retry` in storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py begins with `if getattr(self._request, "__func__", None) is not CloudflareTurnProvider._request: return self._request_without_hedge_retry(payload)`, so any subclass that overrides `_request` skips the hedge. The game's real provider is `storygame.runtime.item_facts.ItemFactsProvider`, which overrides `_request` (it calls `super()._request(payload)` and then post-processes the reply with side effects: `_pending_item_facts`, `item_facts_lifted`, `item_facts_reply_keys`). In a real run a narration call stalled the full 20 s with no second request, and the traceback went `_request_without_hedge_retry` -> `ItemFactsProvider._request` -> `CloudflareTurnProvider._request` -> `_send_http`. The unit tests passed because they only used the base provider.
WHY NOT HEDGE `_request` ITSELF: ItemFactsProvider's override would then run twice concurrently and double-apply its side effects. The hedge must wrap ONLY the raw HTTP send.
FIX. (1) Move the narration hedge to the base `CloudflareTurnProvider._request`: after `_prepare_request` has reserved the budget exactly once, send the narration request through `hedged_call` around `self._send_http(wire_payload)` ONLY (not around budget reservation, `last_prompt`, `_decode_response` or any subclass post-processing), with the existing delay constant `NARRATION_HEDGE_DELAY_S` and `_configured_narration_hedge_delay`, and the shared total deadline = the request timeout. Hedge only when the request budget is `narration`; the `item_facts` budget keeps its own hedge in `_request_item_facts` (do not double-hedge it). A subclass override of `_request` then needs no special casing and post-processes the single winning reply exactly once. (2) Restore `_request_allowing_one_transient_retry` to its pre-hedge behaviour (retry once on a non-timeout connection failure, never on an answered request, never on a timeout) and delete `_request_without_hedge_retry`, the identity guard, `send_raw`, and the `raw` reservation plumbing if nothing else needs them; keep `last_narration_hedge` telemetry if tests or the recorder use it (grep before deleting). Budgets and counters stay logical: one narration request per hedge. (3) Keep `FREYTAG_HEDGE_NARRATION_S=0` disabling narration hedging.
TESTS: rewrite tests/test_narration_hedge.py around the REAL provider: build `ItemFactsProvider` (see how tests/test_bench_item_facts.py or tests/test_item_facts_null_place.py construct one) with `_send_http` replaced by a fake whose first call blocks past the hedge delay and whose second answers at once; assert the second reply is used, exactly one logical narration request is counted (`request_count` / the turn request counters / any `narration_attempts` source), the item-facts post-processing side effects ran ONCE (`item_facts_reply_keys`, `item_facts_lifted`, `_pending_item_facts` set once), and the loser's late reply or exception is swallowed. Also keep: fast reply sends one HTTP request; both slow raises the same timeout error as before within the timeout; an answered HTTPError is not hedged; budgets/counters identical with hedging on and off; `FREYTAG_HEDGE_NARRATION_S=0` restores single-request behaviour; the shared recovery path still makes exactly one recovery request. Add the same fast/slow test for the BASE `CloudflareTurnProvider` too. Update tests/test_cloudflare_transport.py only if the removed plumbing breaks it.
HOW TO VERIFY: run `bash /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/check_t9h_narration_hedge.sh` (it fails if `_request_without_hedge_retry` still exists or the tests do not use ItemFactsProvider). Do not edit it. Final output: a short summary of exactly where the hedge now sits and the proof that the real provider hedges.
